title: Samsung wants to float AI data centres in Texas. The state just froze the grid they need
excerpt: Samsung Heavy Industries and Mousterian will build 50MW floating data centres in Texas, days after the state froze new data-centre grid connections.
content_html:
The floating data centre has moved from concept to contract. Samsung Heavy Industries and the Dallas firm Mousterian have signed an engineering deal to design one, The Register reported. The first project is bound for Texas.

The pitch is a neat answer to the AI buildout’s two tightest constraints: land and water. A moored facility needs no scarce plot. Owners can tow it elsewhere if plans change. And it can draw on the water around it for cooling.

A data centre built like a ship

Mousterian calls itself a developer of water-adjacent data centre infrastructure. The plan is a series of bespoke moored barges, each carrying 50 megawatts of computing capacity. Samsung will bring the shipbuilding.

The two firms will jointly handle the design and detailed engineering, a step towards a full construction contract. The American Bureau of Shipping will classify the facilities, as it would any vessel.

Building in a shipyard is the point. “Because the facility is built in a shipyard, fabrication advances in parallel with sitework rather than after it,” said Mousterian chief executive Min Suh. That, he argued, beats the schedule of a conventional build.

The cooling is the other selling point. Mousterian says its system uses no potable water and pours no discharge back into the waterway. Dropping the usual air chillers and fans, it adds, also cuts the noise. Noise is a big reason neighbours fight data centres on land.

Samsung floats a new line of business

For Samsung Heavy Industries, a shipbuilder, this is a new use for an old skill. It moved into seaborne server farms earlier this year, and last month agreed with Supermicro to test AI servers in river and offshore conditions. Its own first facility is not due until 2028.

“Waterborne server farms are a natural extension of the engineering capabilities the firm has honed over five decades in offshore and maritime construction,” said Samsung Heavy Industries chief executive Sung-an Choi.

The Mousterian pilot is meant to prove a sharper claim: that a floating hall moored next to an existing power plant can come online faster than a conventional site. The first one is understood to sit beside a gas-fired plant in Houston.

The grid had other ideas

That location is the problem. The same week the deal landed, Texas governor Greg Abbott paused new data centre grid connections until regulators audit the queue.

The numbers behind that freeze are startling. Grid operator ERCOT is weighing requests for more than 474 gigawatts of new connections, over five times the state’s peak demand. Data centres account for 90% of them.

Regulators now want each project to say whether it will bring its own power or lean on the grid, and how much water it will use. They will deny a connection to any project that does not answer. A barge moored beside its own gas plant may be better placed than most to pass that test, but nobody has said so yet.

The track record gives reasons for caution. A power-starved industry has floated the idea before, hunting for any way to build faster. Most attempts stalled on the practical problems of running critical kit on water. Rivals are chasing the same land and water elsewhere, from Google in India to a $100bn campus in Kentucky.

Samsung and Mousterian have a design that sidesteps the land and the water. The irony is that their first test sits in the one state that just decided the real bottleneck is the grid.

content_html_zh:
浮动数据中心已从概念转变为合同。 据《The Register》报道，三星重工和达拉斯公司 Mousterian 已签署了一项设计协议。 第一个项目发往德克萨斯州。

此次推介完美地解决了人工智能建设的两个最严格的限制：土地和水。 停泊设施不需要稀缺的土地。 如果计划发生变化，车主可以将其拖到其他地方。 它可以吸收周围的水来冷却。

像船一样建造的数据中心

Mousterian 自称是临水数据中心基础设施开发商。 该计划是一系列定制的停泊驳船，每艘都承载 50 兆瓦的计算能力。 三星将带来造船业。

两家公司将共同处理设计和详细工程，这是迈向完整施工合同的一步。 美国船级社将对这些设施进行分类，就像对任何船只一样。

在造船厂建造是重点。 Mousterian 首席执行官 Min Suh 表示：“由于该设施是在造船厂建造的，因此制造工作与现场施工同步进行，而不是在现场施工之后进行。” 他认为，这超出了传统建设的时间表。

冷却是另一个卖点。 莫斯特里安表示，其系统不使用饮用水，也不会将排放物倒回水道中。 它补充说，放弃常用的空气冷却器和风扇也可以减少噪音。 噪音是邻国与陆地上的数据中心争斗的一个重要原因。

三星推出新业务线

对于造船商三星重工来说，这是一项旧技能的新用途。 该公司今年早些时候进入了海运服务器场，并于上个月与 Supermicro 达成协议，在河流和海上条件下测试人工智能服务器。 它自己的第一个设施要到 2028 年才会建成。

三星重工首席执行官 Sung-an Choi 表示：“水上服务器场是该公司在近海和海事建设领域经过 50 多年磨练的工程能力的自然延伸。”

莫斯特的试点旨在证明一个更尖锐的主张：停泊在现有发电厂旁边的浮动大厅可以比传统站点更快地上线。 据了解，第一个工厂位于休斯敦的一家燃气工厂旁边。

网格还有其他想法

那个位置就是问题所在。 交易达成的同一周，德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特暂停了新的数据中心电网连接，直到监管机构审核队列。

冻结背后的数字令人震惊。 电网运营商 ERCOT 正在权衡超过 474 吉瓦的新连接请求，超过该州峰值需求的五倍。 其中数据中心占90%。

监管机构现在希望每个项目说明是自备电力还是依靠电网，以及将使用多少水。 他们将拒绝与任何不回复的项目建立联系。 停泊在自己的天然气工厂旁边的驳船可能比大多数驳船更容易通过这项测试，但目前还没有人这么说。

往绩记录给出了谨慎的理由。 电力匮乏的行业之前就曾提出过这个想法，并寻求任何加快建设速度的方法。 大多数尝试都停留在用水运行关键套件的实际问题上。 从印度的谷歌到肯塔基州耗资 1000 亿美元的园区，竞争对手们也在其他地方争夺同样的土地和水资源。

三星和莫斯特里安的设计避开了陆地和水域。 讽刺的是，他们的第一个测试是在刚刚确定真正瓶颈是网格的状态下进行的。
